routines.edgeAssessment: Returns and consumes the agent update notification. Registration and writes to watched variables set the flag; unrelated writes do not. Different agents consume independently, and an unregistered agent returns false. kclear affects the pool but registered watches are part of CSPICE process/module state. All registered success cases have observable reads/effects rather than relying on void returns. Added cases use independent fixture-free pool state; read start/room and notification boundaries are tested explicitly.
routines.errorAssessment: Blank identifiers and invalid paging are contract/wrapper validation, not raw CSPICE diagnostic parity. Actual BADVARNAME writes and INTOUTOFRANGE integer conversion are named live errors where applicable. Missing/wrong-type lookups are successful Found/boolean outcomes. Pool/agent exhaustion would require disruptive global-capacity stress rather than a small deterministic semantic fixture; allocation rollback is separately fault-injected at all 43 temporary allocation positions. Null C pointers and undersized output buffers are not reachable through valid typed adapters.
routines.fixtureRationale: No external fixtures or kernels. Distinguishing numeric arrays, ASCII strings, short case-sensitive variable/agent names, and a deliberately overlong variable name are authored in the scenarios; no scientific data or distribution issue.
routines.cleanup: Both workflow runtimes clear the pool around each case and reset error state. CSPICE watch registrations can outlive kclear, so watched names/agents are deterministically reused in self-contained workflows and re-armed/consumed rather than assumed absent; unregistered-agent assertions use a distinct never-registered name. Node process state is serialized; WASM modules isolate cases. Temporary string/data/error buffers are owned by try/finally/withAllocs; 43 failure positions verify rollback before any compiled call. Direct tests kclear and dispose clients in finally.
routines.tolerance: No tolerance changes: integer, boolean, type, string and array-shape comparisons preserve exact values/order; numeric fixtures use binary-exact fractions and compare all values with the existing 1e-12 absolute/relative comparator. gnpool output is deliberately not sorted or normalized.

findings.summary: The first full native run exposed a scenario isolation error: two workflows reused additive agent registrations and a supposedly unrelated write triggered a retained watch. CSPICE watches outlive kclear; fresh WASM modules/Python processes hid this.
findings.repair: Give workflows distinct agents/variables and use a permanently unwatched variable before additive registration. Each state sequence is repeatable with retained registration, rather than assuming kclear unregisters agents. Re-run full native parity without retries or weakened observations.

wasm.trace: Workflow -> kernel-pool dispatcher -> raw.cvpool -> WASM typed adapter and owned temporary buffers -> required compiled _tspice export -> shared tspice_cvpool -> cvpool_c. Oracle directly calls matching SpiceyPy operation; only zero-count pcpool uses its underlying same-named libspice entrypoint because the Python wrapper cannot construct an empty row array.

routines.edgeAssessment: A nonempty signed 32-bit integer write replaces the entire variable with numeric values in stored order, not appending. A zero-count write is a no-op preserving previous state; out-of-range/nonintegral inputs are wrapper errors. Overlong names signal BADVARNAME. All registered success cases have observable reads/effects rather than relying on void returns. Added cases use independent fixture-free pool state; read start/room and notification boundaries are tested explicitly.
routines.errorAssessment: Blank identifiers and invalid paging are contract/wrapper validation, not raw CSPICE diagnostic parity. Actual BADVARNAME writes and INTOUTOFRANGE integer conversion are named live errors where applicable. Missing/wrong-type lookups are successful Found/boolean outcomes. Pool/agent exhaustion would require disruptive global-capacity stress rather than a small deterministic semantic fixture; allocation rollback is separately fault-injected at all 43 temporary allocation positions. Null C pointers and undersized output buffers are not reachable through valid typed adapters.
routines.fixtureRationale: No external fixtures or kernels. Distinguishing numeric arrays, ASCII strings, short case-sensitive variable/agent names, and a deliberately overlong variable name are authored in the scenarios; no scientific data or distribution issue.
routines.cleanup: Both workflow runtimes clear the pool around each case and reset error state. CSPICE watch registrations can outlive kclear, so watched names/agents are deterministically reused in self-contained workflows and re-armed/consumed rather than assumed absent; unregistered-agent assertions use a distinct never-registered name. Node process state is serialized; WASM modules isolate cases. Temporary string/data/error buffers are owned by try/finally/withAllocs; 43 failure positions verify rollback before any compiled call. Direct tests kclear and dispose clients in finally.
routines.tolerance: No tolerance changes: integer, boolean, type, string and array-shape comparisons preserve exact values/order; numeric fixtures use binary-exact fractions and compare all values with the existing 1e-12 absolute/relative comparator. gnpool output is deliberately not sorted or normalized.

findings.summary: Public JSDoc incorrectly claimed empty writes create a size-zero value list. The locked live oracle and both implementations show a no-op preserving an existing variable.
findings.repair: Document actual CSPICE no-op semantics and add live read/type observations before and after zero-count writes, including previous numeric contents before a character write.

findings.summary: The first full native run exposed a scenario isolation error: two workflows reused additive agent registrations and a supposedly unrelated write triggered a retained watch. CSPICE watches outlive kclear; fresh WASM modules/Python processes hid this.
findings.repair: Give workflows distinct agents/variables and use a permanently unwatched variable before additive registration. Each state sequence is repeatable with retained registration, rather than assuming kclear unregisters agents. Re-run full native parity without retries or weakened observations.

findings.summary: WASM iterated plain strings supplied as character/watch arrays, while native correctly rejected non-array inputs. This could mutate pool/watch state using individual characters.
findings.repair: Require actual arrays before validating/encoding character values or watch names; actual-backend boundary tests reject both string arguments before mutation.
